mails.subject: Can you help me with ancienttrees.app? Your Birkelunden photographs
mails.body:
Hi Ingar,

I found two of your photographs of the birches in Birkelunden and think they are lovely! My name is Hidde. I love old trees and being outdoors, and with ancienttrees.app I try to get more people to go outside and visit remarkable trees.

Oslo kommune's park department (Bymiljoetaten) sent them to me and said you took them, so I'd like to ask you directly: may I use them on the Birkelunden page, with your name under the photo?

https://ancienttrees.app/oslo/birches-of-birkelunden

Oslo has no photograph on the site yet, so yours would be the first.

To be open about it: every tree on the site is free to explore, and the app will get a paid subscription for extra features later on. Your photo would stay with the tree, credited to you, and I'd take it down whenever you ask.

And if you know an old tree in Oslo that should be on the list, I'd love to hear which one.

Best,
Hidde
ancienttrees.app

mails.subject: Can you help me with ancienttrees.app? Tord Baklund's Birkelunden photo
mails.body:
Hi,

I found Tord Baklund's photograph of the birches in Birkelunden and think it's a beautiful picture of the park! My name is Hidde. I love old trees and being outdoors, and with ancienttrees.app I try to get more people to go outside and visit remarkable trees, including four in Oslo.

Oslo kommune's park department passed the photo on to me, credited VisitOSLO / Tord Baklund. May I use it on the Birkelunden page, credited exactly that way?

https://ancienttrees.app/oslo/birches-of-birkelunden

To be open about it: every tree on the site is free to explore, and the app will get a paid subscription for extra features later on, so I'd rather ask than assume your image bank terms cover it. I'd take it down whenever you ask.

And if your bank has a photo of Munch-eika in Montebello, Oslo's oldest tree, that would be the one I'd love most.

Best,
Hidde
ancienttrees.app
